title: Delinquency and Cure on Home Mortgage Loans
content:
**Clause 1.** A Home Mortgage Loans note becomes delinquent when an installment is unpaid 30 days after its due date.

**Clause 2.** A delinquent loan returns to active once every past-due installment on it is paid.

**Clause 3.** Foreclosure, short sale and deed-in-lieu decisions lie outside this policy.

## Basis of judgement

| Element | Basis |
|---|---|
| What is measured | An installment left unpaid after its due date |
| The figure it is measured against | 30 days after that due date |
| Where it is read from | The days past due recorded against the loan, correlated to that loan, before the loan is moved to delinquent |
| What returns the loan to active | Every past-due installment on it being paid |

## Both sides of the threshold

Take a hypothetical installment that fell due and has not been paid.

- At 30 days after its due date the loan becomes delinquent.
- At 29 days after its due date it has not yet reached the figure, and the loan has not become delinquent on that installment.

## Points of judgement

The cure is stated of every past-due installment, not of one of them, so a loan carrying two past-due installments returns to active when both have been paid and not when only the older has.
